title: Article 300A — Persons not to be deprived of property save by authority of law

content.overview: Article 300A provides that no person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law. It was inserted by the 44th Amendment after the right to property ceased to be a Fundamental Right (repeal of Art 31 as a FR). It is a constitutional right, not a Fundamental Right under Part III, so it is enforceable under Article 226 but not under Article 32 as a Part III right.
content.glance: No person shall be deprived of property except by authority of law. Constitutional right (not FR); inserted by 44th Amendment after Art 31 ceased to be a Fundamental Right.
content.study:
Article 300A:
- **Text:** No person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law.
- **Status:** Constitutional right outside Part III (44th Amendment). Enforceable by High Courts under Article 226; not by Supreme Court under Article 32 as a Fundamental Right.
- **Content:** Requires legal authority for deprivation; does not restore the full pre-44th Amendment Art 31 compensation/acquisition scheme as a FR, but ‘authority of law’ and related fairness/competence constraints apply.
- **History:** Right to property was a Fundamental Right under Arts 19(1)(f) and 31; 44th Amendment removed it from Part III and enacted Art 300A.

Examination: not a FR; authority of law; 44th Amendment; Art 226 remedy; contrast old Art 31.

sections.heading: Key rules
sections.body:
1. No deprivation of property except by authority of law.
2. Constitutional right, not a Fundamental Right (Part III).
3. Inserted by 44th Amendment after deletion of property as FR.
4. Enforceable under Art 226; not under Art 32 as FR.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the right under Article 300A?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 300A provides that no person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law. It is a constitutional right, not a Fundamental Right under Part III. It was inserted by the Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act after the right to property ceased to be a Fundamental Right. Deprivation of property requires legal authority; the right is enforceable under Article 226 but not under Article 32 as a Part III right.

keyTakeaways: Art 300A: no deprivation of property except by authority of law (constitutional right).
